name: Rajma Madra
subtitle: red kidney beans in a thick soured-yogurt gravy, the dham version that eats richer than chana madra

ingredients.note: the small dark Chamba beans if you can get them
compounded-free hing keeps the dish gluten-free

prepNotes: Soak the rajma at least 10 hours, ideally overnight. Beans that have not swollen to twice their size will not cook through.
Bring the yogurt to room temperature and whisk it with the besan until it pours like thin cream.
Have the whole spices measured into one small bowl - once the ghee is hot they all go in together.

steps.text: Pressure cook the drained rajma with 700ml fresh water and 1 tsp salt for 6 to 7 whistles, then let the pressure fall naturally. A bean should collapse when pressed, with the skin still intact.
steps.tip: Never add the yogurt to half-cooked beans. Acid stops rajma softening dead.

steps.text: Heat the ghee in a heavy pan until it shimmers. Add cumin, black cardamom, green cardamom, cinnamon, cloves and bay leaves; they will foam and smell sweet within 30 to 40 seconds.
Add the asafoetida, then pull the pan off the flame and let it cool a full minute.
steps.tip: Hot ghee plus cold yogurt equals a grainy, broken gravy. The pause is not optional.

steps.text: Return the pan to the lowest heat and pour in the yogurt, stirring without pause for 8 to 10 minutes until it thickens and the raw sourness cooks off.
Stir in the coriander, fennel, dry ginger, turmeric and kashmiri chilli. Cook 3 minutes until the gravy turns a deep ochre and glossy.
Tip in the rajma with about 200ml of its cooking liquor and season with salt.
Crush a small ladleful of the beans against the side of the pan and stir back in - this thickens the gravy without flour.
steps.tip: Six or seven crushed beans is plenty; any more and you lose the texture.

steps.text: Simmer uncovered 25 minutes on low, stirring often, until the ghee separates and rises in a clear rim.
Sprinkle over the garam masala, cover and rest 10 minutes off the heat before serving with steamed rice.

storage: Refrigerates well for 3 days and thickens as it sits. Loosen with hot water and reheat on the lowest flame, stirring; do not let it boil hard or the yogurt will separate.

nutrition.method: Estimated from raw ingredients using USDA FoodData Central. Cooking losses are not modelled and added salt is excluded, so sodium is not given.
